prompt: Why is a carboxylic acid much more acidic (pKa ~4-5) than an alcohol (pKa ~16)?

options.label: The carboxylate conjugate base delocalizes negative charge over TWO equivalent oxygens by resonance
The sp² C in COOH is more electronegative than sp³, pulling electron density off O-H
COOH forms stronger intermolecular H-bonds that pre-polarize the O-H bond
The additional O atom in COOH increases its molecular size, stabilizing the extra charge

explanation: Carboxylate (R-COO⁻) delocalizes the negative charge equally across two oxygens via resonance — enormously stabilizing. Alkoxide (R-O⁻) has nowhere to put the charge. The ~12 pKa gap reflects that resonance stabilization. Induction and H-bonding contribute slightly but resonance dominates.
